action: General advice: shadow maintainer Alejandro Colomar released shadow 4.20.4 with the fix, so update to that release on systems that install newgidmap SUID.
exec: A local flaw in shadow's newgidmap, which a reporter reproduced with a public write-up, is fixed in shadow 4.20.4.
plain: A flaw in newgidmap, part of the shadow tools on Linux, let a local user make the privileged helper write to a file of their choosing. A fixed version, shadow 4.20.4, has been released.

sources.name: oss-security: Re: [PATCH v7 0/2] shadow: Security fix for newgidmap(1) (Alejandro Colomar)
oss-security: Re: Re: [PATCH v7 0/2] shadow: Security fix for newgidmap(1) (Solar Designer)

summary: Shadow maintainer Alejandro Colomar said on oss-security on 22 November that shadow 4.20.4 was released with a fix for newgidmap. The reporter, Dickson Wu, reproduced it on release 4.20.3 with the helper installed SUID and called it a local integrity/DoS issue rather than code execution. Solar Designer's follow-up post cites CVE-2026-135901 and quotes a Red Hat report saying the fix uses openat2(2) with RESOLVE_NO_XDEV.
title: shadow 4.20.4 fixes newgidmap flaw reproduced on 4.20.3

validation.note: Both pages are posts on the oss-security list (one publisher); the maintainer's post states the release. Release notes on GitHub returned 403 and were not read.

evidence.quote: I've released publicly shadow-4.20.4 a moment ago.

review.note: attribution: openat2 statement is a Red Hat report quoted by Solar Designer
